prerequisites: It is recommended to follow the order of the Study Plan to arrive at this discipline with the necessary competencies to address its study.
Mastering the conversions of the most frequent units in science and engineering is critical for passing the subject.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the interactions between different natural environments and the pollutants that affect them.
Understand the sources and entry routes of pollutants into the natural environment.
Understand the legislation affecting each natural environment and its pollutants.
Understand environmental management tools for the control of industrial pollution.
Understand the operation and select the most appropriate technologies and processes to treat emissions, effluents, and waste.

syllabus_topics: Wastewater: pollutants and impacts on the aquatic environment

Treatment and Regeneration of Wastewater (pre-treatment, primary, secondary, tertiary, and quaternary). Sludge line of wastewater treatment plants. Flow diagrams of wastewater treatment plants (WWTP) and regeneration plants (WRTP).
Challenge: Circular Water Management (Zero discharge to the aquatic environment and resource recovery).
Atmospheric Emissions: pollutants and impacts on the atmosphere
Treatment of Atmospheric Emissions: elimination of particles and gaseous pollutants. Flow diagram of gas purification systems.
Challenge: Decarbonization (Zero GHG emissions to the atmosphere).
Waste: concept, classification, coding, and producer obligations.
Waste Treatment: valorization (material and energetic) and elimination.
Challenge: Circular Economy (Zero waste to landfill).
Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Ecodesign. Practical application for the development of low-carbon and circular products.
Standardized Environmental Management Systems for organizations (ISO 14001 and EMAS). Introduction to industrial sustainability metrics (CSRD Directive).
assessment_rules: It is essential to obtain a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 in the Final Exam to be able to average with practical grades. If a student does not pass the Final Exam, only the grades obtained in the computer practicals, laboratory, and field trip activities may be carried over to subsequent calls and even academic years.
